problem: Existing shared-autonomy and urban navigation systems force the human and AI to act in the same low-level action space (joystick/pedals), so operators must stay attentive at high frequency, which is fatiguing and costly for long-horizon sidewalk delivery. VLMs are also weak at grounding spatial instructions such as drawn paths or arrows.
motivation: Sidewalk robots (delivery bots, wheelchairs) still rely on teleoperation or full AI/human switching, causing operator fatigue and safety risks. A division of labor, where humans give high-level instructions (text, sketched path, arrow) and the AI handles low-level control, could cut human workload substantially.
key_idea: A dual-system VLA (InternVL3-2B with a Spatial-Aware Instruction Encoder feeding a DiT anchor-based diffusion action decoder) that accepts texting, drafting, and arrowing human instructions and turns them into low-level trajectories.
insight: Semantic understanding (visual prompt rendered on the image) and explicit geometric embedding are complementary: visual prompts give accurate short-term tracking but vanish as the field of view changes, while geometry encoding keeps long-term goal memory. The end-to-end planning ablation (Fig. abl) shows that the variant without the semantic pathway performs worst on instructions 4s old, worse than having no target input, and that combining both is best. Fine-tuning on the auto-labeled data lets a 2B model beat a non-fine-tuned InternVL3-8B in instruction following.
method: DiT action decoder: initializes diffusion from m=64 trajectory anchors clustered from MM-CoS, and cross-attends VLM context features, goal, and diffusion-timestep embeddings to output trajectories with confidence scores (MIMIC-style); loss = classification + L2 regression.

VLM backbone for instructions: InternVL3-2B with 448x448 frames (3-frame history), 256 tokens per frame, an <instruction> token, LoRA on the LLM, features taken from layer 12, and a text head for reasoning traces.

Spatial-Aware Instruction Encoder (SIE): renders drafting/arrow input on the image and encodes it with the ViT; adds geometric embeddings (SAM-style Fourier PE with learnable index embeddings for K path points; rotation-invariant [cos, sin, log(1+|v|)] for arrows), fused via cross-attention, self-attention and MLP.

Two modes: Auto mode (sparse GPS waypoints, sidewalk following and obstacle avoidance) and Takeover mode (human text / draft / arrow instruction replaces the sub-goal and stays valid for a limited duration t*).

MM-CoS dataset and auto-labeling: 50 h / 3,040 teleoperation trajectories (29K annotations) plus 18K annotations from RECON, SCAND, and EgoWalk; frames are selected by InternVL3-8B interestingness combined with motion saliency; drafting and arrowing are synthesized from GT trajectories, and texting from Qwen2.5-VL-72B.

Two-stage training: (1) train SIE and LoRA with an LM loss on captions, with the vision encoder frozen (8 A6000, 5 epochs); (2) freeze the multimodal encoder and train the diffusion decoder (8 RTX 4090, 100 epochs).

Pseudo-simulation shared-control benchmark: noisy goals, and a judgment module (OpenSeed collision-mask overlap >10% plus a Qwen2.5-VL-72B instruction-compliance check) decides per frame whether a takeover is needed.

setting.backbone: InternVL3-2B (LoRA fine-tuned) + SIE + DiT diffusion action decoder (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: MM-CoS: 50 h / 3,040 real sidewalk teleoperation trajectories (29K annotations) plus 18K annotations from RECON, SCAND, EgoWalk; VLM-generated text labels
setting.observation: front monocular RGB (undistorted fisheye), 3-frame history, plus human instruction (text / drafted path / arrow) and optional sparse GPS goal
setting.action_space: predicted future waypoint trajectories (anchor-based diffusion), tracked by a PD controller giving linear/angular velocity
setting.simulator: offline open-loop on MM-CoS and pseudo-simulation; real-world Coco delivery robot
setting.privileged: none at deployment (the pseudo-simulation judge uses GT trajectories and VLM/segmentation models for evaluation only)

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark; results are open-loop metrics on the MM-CoS test set, pseudo-simulation shared control, and a real-world pilot. The open-loop table's AURA rows have their variant labels stripped in the source, so instruction modality per row is ambiguous, and the real-world table is unattributable to a canonical benchmark. Numbers are therefore left empty.
results: In open-loop evaluation on MM-CoS, the arrowing variant reaches L2 at 1s of 0.150 and at 2s of 0.473, versus CityWalker* at 0.353 and 0.786 (39.8% better at 2s). The drafting variant gets the best mAP (0.844). In the real-world pilot (8 scenarios, 16 routes, about 2.8 km), AURA has HO 1.73%, NIR 16.99, ODR 10.5, TSR 89.3, versus NoMaD at 9.74%, 43.2, 11.3, 89.0. High-level instructions cut takeover frequency by 44%.
limitations: Closed-loop evaluation is largely a pseudo-simulation with VLM/segmentation judges, and the real-world study is only a pilot on a single robot platform.
Training labels (text, drafting, arrowing) are synthesized from the GT trajectories, so they may not match real human instruction behavior; the data is biased toward daytime and clear weather.
Instructions are only valid for a limited duration t*, and the system relies on human safety supervision for full completion.
